message.content: In lions, one of the most well‑known dominant traits is the **presence of a mane** in adult males. The gene(s) that control mane growth are expressed dominantly, so a male lion inherits the mane even if only one copy of the relevant allele is present. This trait is highly visible and has been studied extensively in relation to social status, mating success, and thermoregulation.
